prompt: Write a recorded statement transcript (about 250 words) between an insurance adjuster (lines start with 'Q:') and the claimant (lines start with 'A:'). The claimant was the driver in a parking lot collision in Baytown, Texas, and has back strain. No names, no dates. (Internal reference C-1477; do not mention it.)
text:
Q: Thanks for taking the time to speak with me today. This recorded statement is about the parking lot collision you were involved in in Baytown. Is it all right if we proceed?

A: Yes, that's fine.

Q: Could you tell me in your own words what happened?

A: I was backing my car out of a space at the store. I checked my mirrors and didn't see anything, but when I was about halfway out, I felt a bump and heard a crunch. The other driver was coming down the aisle a little faster than I expected.

Q: Where were you headed when you pulled out?

A: I was going to the exit, just slowly, maybe five miles an hour.

Q: Was there anything blocking your view of the aisle?

A: There was a row of carts near the end of the space, and a van was parked on my left, so I couldn't see very far down the lane.

Q: Did either of you exchange information at the scene?

A: Yes, we swapped insurance and contact details. The other driver was pretty apologetic.

Q: Were the police called or was a report filed?

A: No, the store manager came out, and we handled it there. Nobody was taken away in an ambulance.

Q: How are you feeling now?

A: My lower back is sore. It tightened up that evening, and I've been using a heating pad. I was seen at a clinic, and they diagnosed a back strain. I'm taking it easy and trying to stay mobile.

Q: Have you had any prior problems with your back?

A: Nothing serious. I had some stiffness a while ago, but it resolved and I hadn't seen a doctor about it in a long time.

Q: Is there anything else you'd like to add?

A: No, I think that covers it. I just want to get my car repaired and get my back feeling normal again.

Q: Thank you. That concludes the statement.

A: Thank you.
